name: Kamal Hossain
role: Lawyer; chaired Bangladesh's constitution drafting committee
connection: Dr. Hossain met Kamal Hossain in Dhaka in 1963 and married him in 1964. He was publisher of Forum when she edited it, and later argued public interest cases for Ain o Salish Kendra. In 1998 she went with him on his UN mission to Afghanistan.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Sara Hossain
role: Barrister; Dr. Hossain's elder daughter
connection: Sara Hossain is the elder of Dr. Hossain's two daughters, born in Dhaka in the late 1960s. Mother and daughter co-authored a report, Women and the Legal System, with Neela Matin.

name: Dina Hossain
role: Documentary filmmaker and teacher; younger daughter
connection: Dina Hossain is the younger of Dr. Hossain's two daughters. She shared the family's years in Karachi in 1971 and in Oxford after 1975, and later put questions to her mother about the Oxford years for the memoir.
source: timeline.json; 04 Memoir/09 Oxford Years/Dina- Questions Oxford Years.docx

name: Iqbal Akhund
role: Pakistani diplomat; Dr. Hossain's eldest brother
connection: Iqbal Akhund was the eldest of the six Akhund children, born like Dr. Hossain in Hyderabad, Sindh. Her memoir recalls him as the brother who taught the younger ones and settled their childhood quarrels.

name: Rehman Sobhan
role: Economist; executive editor of Forum
connection: Dr. Hossain met Rehman Sobhan in Dhaka in 1963. When Forum began in November 1969 he was its executive editor and she its editor, working from a garage room on Circuit House Road until the March 1971 crackdown. She also wrote a chapter for The Decade of Stagnation, which he edited.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Khan Sarwar Murshid
role: Professor of English; editor of New Values
connection: On her first visit to Dhaka in 1963, Dr. Hossain heard Dr Murshid in the university teachers' debates. He invited her to help edit an issue of his humanist journal New Values, work she later called her political education.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Kamruddin Ahmad
role: Lawyer, writer; Language Movement figure
connection: Dr. Hossain met Kamruddin Ahmad through her work on New Values in 1960s Dhaka. She names him among the scholars there who took part in the labour movement and the Language Movement.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Professor Abdur Razzaq
role: Political scientist; National Professor
connection: Dr. Hossain knew Professor Razzaq, 'Sir', from her first years in Dhaka. He walked her through the city's markets, urged her to learn Persian for her weavers research, and brought her into the circle of scholars and artists who met at his home. She credits him with shaping her thesis.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Anisuzzaman
role: Scholar of Bangla literature
connection: Dr. Hossain first heard Anisuzzaman in the Dhaka University teachers' room in the 1960s, and he then taught her Bangla at the Bangla Academy, in a class she joined with Salma Sobhan. Years later, in the India Office Library in London, his translations of East India Company Bangla records fed into her thesis on Bengal's weavers.

works.label: Memories of My Encounters with Anisuzzaman

name: Rounaq Jahan
role: Political scientist; founder of Women for Women
connection: Dr. Hossain and Rounaq Jahan met in 1970 at Professor Razzaq's gatherings and stayed friends for some fifty years. Rounaq Jahan encouraged her to go to the 1975 UN women's conference in Mexico, and they later met again at DAWN, APWLD and other feminist networks.

works.label: A Tribute to My Friend Rounaq Jahan

name: Razia Khan Amin
role: Writer, poet and teacher of English
connection: Dr. Hossain met Razia Khan Amin after moving to Dhaka and remembers her speaking for women's demands at neighbourhood meetings and rallies. Razia Khan also wrote literary criticism for Forum.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Salma Sobhan
role: Barrister and law teacher; co-founder of ASK
connection: Dr. Hossain and Salma Sobhan learned Bangla together at the Bangla Academy in the 1960s. Back from exile in Oxford, they co-founded Ain o Salish Kendra in 1986, and with Roushan Jahan they co-wrote No Better Option?, a study of women industrial workers.

works.label: Remarks at the SAJIDA Foundation Conference
The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: M. Amir-ul Islam
role: Barrister; co-founder of ASK
connection: Barrister Amirul Islam was one of the founders of Ain o Salish Kendra with Dr. Hossain and later sat on its executive committee. He took up the Yasmin case in 1995 and moved ASK's petition against the Taltola slum eviction.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: F. H. Abed
role: Founder of BRAC; co-founder of ASK
connection: F. H. Abed was among the founders of Ain o Salish Kendra with Dr. Hossain. After the 1991 cyclone they co-edited, with Cole P. Dodge, From Crisis to Development: Coping with Disasters in Bangladesh.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Asma Jahangir
role: Pakistani human-rights lawyer; first co-chair of SAHR
connection: Dr. Hossain and Asma Jahangir became close friends while working with other activists to form South Asians for Human Rights, of which Asma was the first co-chair, and through the Asia Pacific Forum on Women, Law and Development. Dr. Hossain wrote two tributes after her death in 2018.

name: I. K. Gujral
role: Former Prime Minister of India; SAHR chairperson
connection: I. K. Gujral was among SAHR's founders at Neemrana in 2000 and its chairperson while Dr. Hossain was co-chairperson (2008–11). In her 2010 welcome addresses she noted that, though too unwell to attend, he went on counselling the network.

works.label: Welcome Address: SAHR Conference, New Delhi

name: Sultana Kamal
role: Lawyer and rights activist; led ASK
connection: Sultana Kamal was on the team that recorded women's oral histories of 1971 for Ain o Salish Kendra, and she sat with Dr. Hossain on the editorial board of Rising from the Ashes. She is the daughter of Begum Sufia Kamal.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Khushi Kabir
role: Activist; coordinator of Nijera Kori
connection: Dr. Hossain and Khushi Kabir went together to court hearings in Jhalakathi for Limon, a boy shot by RAB whose case ASK took up. They also spoke on the same 2021 Harvard panel on women in Bangladesh at fifty.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Begum Sufia Kamal
role: Poet; president of Bangladesh Mahila Parishad
connection: Dr. Hossain was in the audience in 1970 when Sufia Kamal spoke at the founding of the Mahila Parishad. In 1972 she volunteered at the Women's Rehabilitation Centre Sufia Kamal helped set up, and later worked with the Parishad on CEDAW shadow reports.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Ayesha Khanam
role: Women's-rights leader; Mahila Parishad president
connection: Dr. Hossain first saw Ayesha Khanam as a student marching in 1969. Through ASK and the Mahila Parishad they worked together on a Uniform Family Code, the Yasmin and Nurjahan cases, and CEDAW shadow reports, attending the 2004 CEDAW hearing in New York together and co-writing the report on it.

name: Jahanara Imam
role: Writer; led the campaign to try war criminals
connection: When Jahanara Imam's movement held the People's Tribunal in 1992, Dr. Hossain and her colleagues at ASK responded by recording oral histories of women survivors of 1971, which were published as Narir Ekattor and Rising from the Ashes.

name: Shirin Akhtar
role: Founder of Kormojibi Nari; trade unionist, MP
connection: Dr. Hossain came to know Shirin Akhtar in the 1980s movement against Ershad. ASK and Kormojibi Nari later studied lay-offs together, took up the Yasmin and Shima cases, and went to the KTS factory fire victims, and both groups joined the Sramik Nirapotta Forum.

name: Shireen Huq
role: Women's-rights activist; founder of Naripokkho
connection: Shireen Huq and Dr. Hossain were co-panellists at the Mittal South Asia Institute's 2021 Bangladesh at 50 conference, on a panel about women's empowerment moderated by Marty Chen.

name: Naila Kabeer
role: Social economist at the LSE
connection: Naila Kabeer spoke with Dr. Hossain on the 2021 Bangladesh at 50 panel on women's empowerment at Harvard's Mittal South Asia Institute.

name: Kamla Bhasin
role: Indian feminist activist and writer
connection: Dr. Hossain met Kamla Bhasin through the UN women's conferences and counted her a close friend. In the 1990s she attended a feminist meeting in Bangalore that Kamla Bhasin organised, where women from across the region spoke out against war.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Nighat Said Khan
role: Pakistani feminist; founder of ASR Resource Centre
connection: Nighat Said Khan suggested the 'Herstory' theme of the women's peace conference where Dr. Hossain gave her talk. Dr. Hossain recalls her as the first Pakistani to come to Dhaka and say that Pakistan must apologise for 1971.

name: Kumari Jayawardena
role: Sri Lankan feminist scholar
connection: Kumari Jayawardena wrote for Forum when Dr. Hossain edited it, and the two became friends through the regional feminist circle that grew after the 1975 Mexico conference. In her Herstory talk, Dr. Hossain recalls Kumari protesting outside the Pakistani embassy in Colombo in 1971.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society
A Tribute to My Friend Rounaq Jahan

name: Ferdousi Priyabhashini
role: Sculptor; spoke publicly as a Birangona
connection: Ferdousi Priyabhashini was one of the first women interviewed for ASK's oral histories of 1971. Dr. Hossain names her as one of the women whose testimony reminded her why citizens' activism matters.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Nurjahan Murshid
role: Journalist, teacher and cabinet minister
connection: Dr. Hossain met Nurjahan Murshid among the women voicing women's demands in 1960s Dhaka. In the 1980s she lent Ain o Salish Kendra the garage in Dhanmondi that became its first office.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Patua Qamrul Hasan
role: Painter; first president of the National Crafts Council
connection: Dr. Hossain knew Qamrul Hasan from the 1960s. When the National Crafts Council of Bangladesh formed in 1985, with him as its first president, she served as its secretary, and together they organised a crafts exhibition in London.

name: Zainul Abedin
role: Painter; known as Shilpacharya
connection: Zainul Abedin, with Professor Razzaq, introduced Dr. Hossain to the visual arts of East Bengal. After independence she set up the KARIKA crafts cooperative with his advice, and she keeps a 200-year-old kantha he gave her as a token of their friendship.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Jasleen Dhamija
role: Indian textile historian and crafts expert
connection: Dr. Hossain met Jasleen Dhamija on the flight to the 1975 UN women's conference in Mexico, and the two spoke on the same crafts panel there. She became a friend and mentor, and Dr. Hossain kept up links between craft groups in Bangladesh, India and Mexico.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Devaki Jain
role: Indian feminist economist
connection: Dr. Hossain met Devaki Jain on the way to the 1975 Mexico conference, and she has been a close friend since. Devaki Jain invited her to the DAWN meeting held to prepare for the 1985 Nairobi conference.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society
A Tribute to My Friend Rounaq Jahan

name: Tapan Raychaudhuri
role: Historian; her Oxford doctoral supervisor
connection: Tapan Raychaudhuri supervised Dr. Hossain's DPhil at St Antony's College, Oxford. He encouraged her to take her work with living weavers back into the historical records, which became The Company Weavers of Bengal.
source: timeline.json; 03 Interviews/BDI Newsletter Interview – Questions (12 Mar 2021).docx; 04 Memoir

name: Helen Hiett Waller
role: Journalist; director of the Herald Tribune Forum
connection: Helen Hiett Waller ran the New York Herald Tribune Forum for high-school students, where Dr. Hossain represented Pakistan in 1952. Her recommendation helped Dr. Hossain win a scholarship to Wellesley College.

works.label: Timeline: Herald Tribune Forum and Wellesley

name: Amena Mohsin
role: Professor of international relations, Dhaka University
connection: Dr. Hossain and Amena Mohsin co-edited Of the Nation Born: The Bangladesh Papers (2016) and its expanded Bangla edition, Ekti Jatir Janma (2018). Dr. Hossain also reviewed Amena Mohsin's study of women and violent extremism.

works.label: Review: The Role of Women in Preventing Violent Extremism

name: Meghna Guhathakurta
role: Scholar; executive director of Research Initiatives Bangladesh
connection: Meghna Guhathakurta worked with Dr. Hossain on ASK's 1971 oral histories and on the editorial board of Rising from the Ashes. She co-wrote Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want? with her and Malini Sur, introduced Of the Nation Born, and co-edited Gendered Lives, to which Dr. Hossain contributed.

works.label: Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want?

name: Malini Sur
role: Anthropologist, Western Sydney University
connection: Malini Sur co-wrote Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want? Re-thinking Security in Bangladesh (2010) with Dr. Hossain and Meghna Guhathakurta.

works.label: Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want?

name: Roushan Jahan
role: Researcher on women; led Women for Women
connection: Roushan Jahan co-wrote No Better Option? Industrial Women Workers in Bangladesh with Dr. Hossain and Salma Sobhan, from a study they carried out in 1987. She was the elder sister of Rounaq Jahan.

links.label: Centre for Policy Dialogue (tribute by Rounaq Jahan)

name: Ayesha Banu
role: Professor of Women and Gender Studies, Dhaka University
connection: Ayesha Banu co-edited Gendered Lives, Livelihood and Transformation (2017), which includes a chapter by Dr. Hossain and Suraiya Begum. She also interviewed Dr. Hossain in Bangla in 2019.
source: books.json; 03 Interviews & Writings about HH/Interview with Dr Hameeda Hossain by Dr Ayesha Banu (19 Sep 2019)

name: Imtiaz Ahmed
role: Professor of international relations, Dhaka University
connection: Imtiaz Ahmed edited Human Rights in Bangladesh: Past, Present and Future (2014), for which Dr. Hossain wrote Chapter 5, 'Human Rights in the Nation State'.

works.label: Human Rights in Bangladesh: Past, Present and Future

name: Niaz Zaman
role: Writer, translator; professor of English
connection: Niaz Zaman translated ASK's Bangla oral histories of 1971 into English as Rising from the Ashes, the volume Dr. Hossain helped edit and wrote the foreword for.

name: Ashfaq Swapan
role: Writer and journalist; translator
connection: Ashfaq Swapan translated Dr. Hossain's remembrance of Anisuzzaman into Bangla.

name: Cole P. Dodge
role: UNICEF Representative in Bangladesh (early 1990s)
connection: After the 1991 cyclone, Cole P. Dodge co-edited From Crisis to Development: Coping with Disasters in Bangladesh (1992) with Dr. Hossain and F. H. Abed.

name: Suraiya Begum
role: Researcher; oral historian of 1971
connection: Suraiya Begum was on the ASK team that gathered women's oral histories of 1971 and sat with Dr. Hossain on the editorial board of Rising from the Ashes. The two also co-wrote a chapter in Gendered Lives.

works.label: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

name: Ghulam Fatima Shaikh
role: Dr. Hossain's maternal grandmother; founder of a girls' school in Hyderabad, Sindh
connection: Ghulam Fatima Shaikh was born into a Hindu Amil family of Sindh that converted to Islam, and married Shaikh Shamsuddin as a girl. She trained as a midwife in Delhi and went with her family to Turkey, Madinah and Syria in the years of the First World War. Hameeda was born in her house in Hyderabad in 1936. In 1947 she turned an abandoned house near the railway station into a shelter and hospital for refugees and enlisted the eleven-year-old Hameeda to help. The same year she founded the Fatima Girls Middle School, which she ran until her death in 1981. Dr. Hossain wrote about her life as a student at Wellesley, and her oral memoir was published as Footprints in Time, translated by her granddaughter Rasheeda Husain.

name: Judge Akhund
role: Her father; a judge in Sindh and Khairpur State
connection: Dr. Hossain's father served as a judge in towns across Sindh, among them Sukkur, Nawabshah, Shikarpur and Larkana, and later joined the judicial service of Khairpur State, where he heard cases arising from the Hur uprising of the early 1940s. He kept a diary, told the children adventure stories and folk tales, and wanted them to have a modern education, sending the six of them to convent and missionary schools in Karachi. In 1971 Dr. Hossain and her daughters lived with her parents in Karachi while Kamal Hossain was imprisoned.

name: Mariam Akhund (née Shaikh)
role: Dr. Hossain's mother
connection: Mariam Akhund was the daughter of Ghulam Fatima and Shaikh Shamsuddin. Married at seventeen, she went with her first child, Iqbal, to her mother in Delhi and learned English at St Mary's Convent there. She later moved the six children to Karachi so they could go to school, and raised them between Karachi and Hyderabad. In 1971 Dr. Hossain and her daughters lived with her parents at their Karachi home in the Sindhi Muslim Housing Society.

name: Rasheeda Husain (née Akhund)
role: Teacher, broadcaster and translator; Dr. Hossain's eldest sister
connection: Rasheeda was the eldest of the Akhund sisters, about eight years older than Hameeda. With Iqbal she took charge of the younger children's lessons during holidays, and she shared her boarding room at St Joseph's Convent in Karachi with her youngest sister. She married Akhlaque Hussain and lived in Dhaka in the early 1960s, then in Karachi, where in 1971 she and Dr. Hossain shared the family house. She worked as a teacher, newsreader, radio music presenter, research librarian and publicity manager, and translated from Sindhi and annotated their grandmother's memoir, Footprints in Time (Oxford University Press). She also wrote her own reminiscences of the family's childhood.

name: Khursheed Erfan Ahmed
role: Educator and counsellor; co-founder of Ain o Salish Kendra; Dr. Hossain's sister
connection: Khursheed Erfan Ahmed taught in Hyderabad, Sindh, in the early 1950s and was the first woman secretary of the Sind University students' union. After her marriage to Erfan Ahmed she settled in Dhaka, and it was on a visit to her home in 1963 that Dr. Hossain met Rehman Sobhan and Kamal Hossain. The sisters worked together with the Srijani women's craft cooperative and the Arunima artisans' outlet in the 1960s, and both were among the founders of Ain o Salish Kendra in 1986. At ASK she directed education and training, prepared legal literacy materials, started the Jokhon Tokhon schools for working children and brought psychosocial counselling into its work. Dr. Hossain thanks her in Claiming Our Rights.

role: Medical doctor; Dr. Hossain's brother

role: Dr. Hossain's brother, two years her senior
connection: Rafiq was the brother closest in age to Hameeda. They went to school in Karachi as children and travelled together to Karachi with their sisters days before Partition in 1947. He took part in the discussions that led to Forum and read and commented on its articles, though he did not join it formally. In 1970 he was posted as ambassador to Tunisia. Dr. Hossain wrote a memoir piece about him and his quiet efforts for a negotiated settlement before 1971.
